sections.html:
This Palm Springs is a village in central Palm Beach County, not the California desert city. It was chartered by the 1957 legislature on about 700 acres of pastureland with a dairy barn and no residents. By August 1958 the first section opened with some 800 homes on paved, landscaped streets.

The village now has about 28,000 residents and a mix of single-family homes, townhomes, apartments and condominiums. A 1960s ranch, a townhouse and a condo each sell to a different buyer, and condo or townhome sellers should line up association paperwork early.

The village runs along Congress Avenue south to Lake Worth Road, west to Military Trail and north along the east side of Military Trail to Forest Hill Boulevard. It extends east toward Florida Mango Road and south along it to 10th Avenue North. Congress Avenue and Lake Worth Road anchor the commercial areas.

A Community Redevelopment Agency works on older commercial areas, streetscapes and walkability. Redevelopment is a selling point for some buyers, so ask the village what projects are planned near your street.

Your bill follows one yearly cycle: the county values the house on January 1 and mails bills in November.

Florida property tax dates that apply in Palm Springs
DateWhat happens
January 1Assessment date
March 1Exemption filing deadline
AugustProposed tax (TRIM) notice mailed
NovemberTax bills sent, 4 percent discount for payment that month
April 1Unpaid taxes delinquent

To dispute your value, file a petition with the clerk within 25 days of the TRIM notice. The county appraiser can walk you through your parcel and any exemptions.

Your permanent home can qualify for as much as $50,000 in exemption, applied for on Form DR-501 by March 1. Under Save Our Homes, assessed value grows each year by the smaller of 3 percent or CPI, and the state chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026.

After a sale the buyer begins at just value. Owners of many years are often surprised how much higher the buyer's bill can run. Have a lender or agent estimate it instead of quoting yours to a buyer.

The deed carries a stamp tax of 70 cents on every $100, and the statute includes any mortgage or encumbrance on the property in the amount taxed.

  • Recording with the clerk costs $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each page after it.
  • Names past the fourth cost $1.00 apiece.
  • Extra modernization and technology charges apply per page.

The closing agent adds these up. Transfers made for estate planning get no special stamp exemption.

sections.h2: Repairs and permits before you sell
sections.html:
A house from the late 1950s or 1960s may need a new roof, wiring, plumbing or windows before an insurer or lender relaxes. Investors can take on that risk. A buyer with a loan may ask you to do the work first.

Ask the village building office what permits exist for earlier work, and keep invoices and inspection records. Permits that were never closed usually come out during title review.

A bill goes delinquent April 1 and a certificate is sold by June 1. The certificate holder cannot press the owner for payment for two years after April 1 of the issue year, and applying for a tax deed costs $75.

The clerk runs the auction. The winning bidder puts down a nonrefundable deposit of $200 or 5 percent, whichever is larger, and pays the balance within a day, skipping weekends and holidays. A sale before the auction removes the risk.

  • A homestead with under $250 delinquent goes to the county and not to auction.
  • Notice of a tax deed goes to the titleholder, any mortgagee and any contract for deed buyer.

When strangers are in a house and there is no tenancy, no family tie and no court case, the owner can sign a complaint asking the sheriff to remove them. A false statement in it can cost the owner damages, including triple the fair market rent.

A claim of adverse possession requires seven years of possession and tax payments, and moving in on that theory before the return is filed is trespass. Check on a vacant house often and keep it locked.

A landlord may mail a notice, hand it over, e-mail it where the statute allows, or leave it at the unit if the tenant is away. A lease cannot waive these rules.

After a ruling for the landlord, the sheriff posts 24 hours of notice and then returns possession. A tenant defending on any ground besides payment has 5 days to deposit rent with the court or forfeit those defenses. Month-to-month tenancies end on 30 days' notice, and a lease that stays in place will shape the offers you get.

A land deed must be written and signed with two witnesses, which your title agent arranges along with recording. Before that point, you compare offers and pick a buyer.

  • Put in the contract who pays doc stamps and recording.
  • Ask your lender for a payoff letter if a mortgage remains.
  • Check the tax roll for liens and exemption status.
  • Be available for a walkthrough if the buyer brings an inspector.

Call the Village of Palm Springs for questions about permits, code compliance and rental rules on your street.

sections.h2: Inherited homes and houses behind on payments
sections.html: State rules fix the steps for inherited homes and houses behind on payments. A small estate (under $150,000 non-exempt) may use summary administration, and unpaid rent begins with a 3 day notice. A foreclosure auction follows the judgment by 20 to 35 days. If payments are behind, call your lender early. Selling before the auction can let you keep equity that a foreclosure sale would take.

sections.h2: What to bring when you meet a buyer
sections.html: Have the deed or your last closing papers, the most recent tax bill, a payoff figure if a mortgage remains, and a list of repairs and permits from the past years. For a rental, add the lease and rent records. A buyer who sees these up front can make a firm offer and the title agent can start sooner. Walk the house yourself first and note anything an inspector will find, such as an old roof or aging wiring, so you can price it into the sale or tell the buyer plainly. If the village or the county has sent any notice about the property, bring that too, and pay or resolve it before you sign so it does not hold up the closing.

For a unit inside an association, ask for its sale rules and estoppel paperwork the day you decide to sell. Some associations must approve the buyer, and that step can push back closing. Cash buyers usually clear it quickly, yet the forms are identical, so begin before you accept an offer. Know your monthly dues and any special assessment, because buyers ask for both.

faqs.q: Is Palm Springs, FL the same as the California city?
faqs.a: No. It is a village in Palm Beach County chartered in 1957, with about 28,000 residents.

faqs.q: When do Palm Beach County tax bills arrive?
faqs.a: In November, under the state calendar. Taxes unpaid after the year turns become delinquent on April 1.

faqs.q: Is there a state tax on the deed in Palm Springs?
faqs.a: Yes. Documentary stamp tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, collected by the clerk at recording.
Yes. Petition the clerk within 25 days of the TRIM notice, which arrives in August.

faqs.q: What if my condo has association approval rules?
faqs.a: Request the association's sale rules early, because approval timing can move the closing date.
